content.p: This Act is the Australian Organ and Tissue Donation and Transplantation Authority Amendment (Disclosure of Information) Act 2023.

Each provision of this Act specified in column 1 of the table commences, or is taken to have commenced, in accordance with column 2 of the table. Any other statement in column 2 has effect according to its terms.

tr.td: A single day to be fixed by Proclamation. However, if the provisions do not commence within the period of 6 months beginning on the day this Act receives the Royal Assent, they commence on the day after the end of that period.

content.p: Note: This table relates only to the provisions of this Act as originally enacted. It will not be amended to deal with any later amendments of this Act.
Any information in column 3 of the table is not part of this Act. Information may be inserted in this column, or information in it may be edited, in any published version of this Act.

Legislation that is specified in a Schedule to this Act is amended or repealed as set out in the applicable items in the Schedule concerned, and any other item in a Schedule to this Act has effect according to its terms.

In this Act, authorised family member of an organ or tissue donor or recipient who has died means any of the following persons:
the partner of the organ or tissue donor or recipient;
a parent or legal guardian of the organ or tissue donor or recipient;
a child of the organ or tissue donor or recipient;
a sibling of the organ or tissue donor or recipient;
a grandparent of the organ or tissue donor or recipient;
a grandchild of the organ or tissue donor or recipient;

if the organ or tissue donor or recipient has traditional Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander kinship ties—a person who is related to the organ or tissue donor or recipient under Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander kinship rules;

if the organ or tissue donor or recipient is a member of a community that accepts relationships other than those referred to in paragraphs (a) to (g) as kinship ties—a person who is accepted by the community to be related to the organ or tissue donor or recipient;
a person who, under the regulations, is taken to be an authorised family member of the organ or tissue donor or recipient.
(1) In this Act, partner of a person means:
the person’s spouse; or
the person’s de facto partner.

(2) However, if more than one person would qualify as a partner of a person (the first person) under subsection (1), then only the last person to so qualify is the partner of the first person for the purposes of this Act.
(1) In this Act, child of a person includes:
an adopted child, stepchild, exnuptial child or foster child of the person; and
(b) someone who is a child of the person within the meaning of the Family Law Act 1975.
Tracing family relationships

For the purposes of this Act, if one person is the child of another person because of subsection (1), relationships traced to or through that person are to be determined on the basis that the person is the child of the other person.
Without limiting who is a parent of a person for the purposes of this Act, a person (the first person) is a parent of another person if the other person is the first person’s child.
In this Act, sibling of a person includes a half-brother, half-sister, adoptive brother, adoptive sister, step-brother, step-sister, foster-brother and foster-sister of the person.

In this Act, without limiting who is a stepchild of a person, a person (the first person) is a stepchild of another person (the second person) if the first person would be the second person’s stepchild except that the second person is not legally married to the second person’s de facto partner.
(1) The Minister may, by legislative instrument, declare that a specified agency is a DonateLife Agency for the purposes of this Act.

(2) The Minister must not declare under subsection (1) that an agency is a DonateLife Agency unless the Minister is satisfied that the agency has a role or function in relation to one or more organ or tissue donation and transplantation matters.

section.heading: Publication, dissemination or disclosure of patient information—DonateLife Agencies, grant recipients and authorised family members

content.p: Scope
This section applies if:
an organ or tissue donation and transplantation has occurred; and
the organ or tissue donor or recipient has died.
Publication, dissemination or disclosure by a DonateLife Agency or grant recipient
Either of the following:
a DonateLife Agency;
a person who is a party to an agreement that:
is in force; and
provides for the making of one or more grants under paragraph 11(1)(g) to the person;
may publish, disseminate or disclose information that is likely to enable the identification of the deceased organ or tissue donor or the deceased organ or tissue recipient (as the case requires) if:
the publication, dissemination or disclosure is for the purposes of any of the following activities:
an educational activity that is relevant to an organ or tissue donation and transplantation matter;
a commemorative activity that is an organ or tissue donation and transplantation matter;
a promotional activity that is relevant to an organ or tissue donation and transplantation matter;
a community awareness activity that is relevant to an organ or tissue donation and transplantation matter; and
(d) the publication, dissemination or disclosure is made with the consent of an authorised family member of the deceased organ or tissue donor or recipient; and
the publication, dissemination or disclosure is made:
using a service to which paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution applies; or
(ii) using an electronic service (within the meaning of the Online Safety Act 2021); or
in a Territory; or
(iv) in a Commonwealth place (within the meaning of the Commonwealth Places (Application of Laws) Act 1970); or
by a constitutional corporation.
Publication, dissemination or disclosure by an authorised family member

An authorised family member of the deceased organ or tissue donor or recipient may publish, disseminate or disclose information that is likely to enable the identification of the deceased organ or tissue donor or the deceased organ or tissue recipient (as the case requires) if:
the publication, dissemination or disclosure is for the purposes of any of the following activities of the Authority or a DonateLife Agency:
an educational activity that is relevant to an organ or tissue donation and transplantation matter;
a commemorative activity that is an organ or tissue donation and transplantation matter;
a promotional activity that is relevant to an organ or tissue donation and transplantation matter;
a community awareness activity that is relevant to an organ or tissue donation and transplantation matter; and
the publication, dissemination or disclosure is made:
using a service to which paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution applies; or
(ii) using an electronic service (within the meaning of the Online Safety Act 2021); or
in a Territory; or
(iv) in a Commonwealth place (within the meaning of the Commonwealth Places (Application of Laws) Act 1970).
Subsections (2) and (3) have effect despite anything in a law of a State or Territory.
Secondary publication, dissemination or disclosure
If information has been the subject of a publication, dissemination or disclosure under subsection (2) or (3), a person may publish, disseminate or disclose that information if:
the publication, dissemination or disclosure is for the purposes of reporting on any of the following activities:
an educational activity that is relevant to an organ or tissue donation and transplantation matter;
a commemorative activity that is an organ or tissue donation and transplantation matter;
a promotional activity that is relevant to an organ or tissue donation and transplantation matter;
a community awareness activity that is relevant to an organ or tissue donation and transplantation matter; and
the publication, dissemination or disclosure is made:
using a service to which paragraph 51(v) of the Constitution applies; or
(ii) using an electronic service (within the meaning of the Online Safety Act 2021); or
in a Territory; or
(iv) in a Commonwealth place (within the meaning of the Commonwealth Places (Application of Laws) Act 1970).
Subsection (5) has effect despite anything in a law of a State or Territory.
